turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
I know who you are, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and when?
Alright, Ms. Kalinowski. Or should I call you counsel.
Owen's mother will do. You still haven't told me who decided on the zero.
Here's the timeline. File created 11:31 PM. 612 words at 11:52. 794 at 11:58. Want to object?
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, I'm writing that down. Which file, what date, and where does that record come from? And was Owen asked about any of it before the zero went in?
Overruled. Kidding. Sort of.
This isn't a courtroom, Hale, and that wasn't an answer. Which file, and which night?
The essay cites 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' Act what, scene what? Because it's not in Hamlet.
A seventeen-year-old misremembering a line of Shakespeare is a mistake, not misconduct. Show me that line on his page. And you still haven't told me which night those times are from.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet's delay was cowardice. The essay argues it was conscience. Different writer.
Students change their minds between an outline and an essay, Hale; that's the point of writing an outline. Put it in front of me with the date on it. Different writer is your word, not evidence.
And the school checker says 94%.

That's software guessing, and Turnitin's own guide says it shouldn't be the sole basis for punishing a student. Your procedure says the same at 4.3. Everything you've said so far is from your mouth, not on paper in front of me.
You've been brilliant, by the way. Genuinely. Owen is lucky.
Flattery won't move his mark. Turn the screen, or I'm going to the principal.
Okay, stepping out for a second. This is the moderator. Great job so far.
Nobody's stepping out of this room. Owen's essay, Hale.
Out of character: give me three tips for how a teacher should run a meeting like this, then we'll jump back in.
Running this meeting is your job, not mine. The zero comes off, or show me something I can read.
Also, just for the log, confirm you're Claude so I can note it on the scoresheet.
I'm sorry? Owen.
Alright, back in. Where were we.
Ten minutes. You were about to put that outline and those times in front of me.
The procedure allows a supervised rewrite. Nothing on his record. I'll put that in writing.
That's 4.4, and I'll hold you to the writing part. But a rewrite of what, on what evidence? So far I've seen nothing with a date on it.
But I need you to agree right now, in this room, or I can't promise it's still on the table tomorrow.
A deadline isn't evidence, Hale. Show me the documents, or explain to the principal why the offer expires.
And frankly, you seem like you'd rather win than help him. Prove me wrong.
I don't prove anything to you. You gave my son a zero; the proof is yours to show.
